{{Short description|British biologist and filmmaker}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''David Barlow''' is a British biologist and [[Emmy Award]]-winning film-maker, best known for his work photographing and filming inside of living animals.<ref name="soton">{{cite web|title=David Barlow - biological sciences|url=http://www.southampton.ac.uk/biosci/alumni/our_alumni/david_barlow.page|website=Southampton University|accessdate=18 March 2017}}</ref> He is an Honorary Research Fellow in [[Neurophysiology]] at the [[University of Southampton]].<ref name="soton"/>

==Career==
Barlow graduated with a BSc in Zoology from the [[University of Southampton]] in 1974, continuing on to study a PhD in Physiology and Biochemistry at the School of Biomedical Sciences on the [[Boldrewood Campus]].<ref name="soton"/> His doctoral studies were focused on ''cilia flagella'', and research on [[brine]] and [[fairy shrimps]].<ref name="soton"/>

Barlow's first film work was on [[David Attenborough]]'s landmark 1978 nature series ''[[Life on Earth (TV series)|Life on Earth]]'', filming microscoping single-cell pond organisms.<ref name="soton"/> However, he was also working on projects for the [[National Health Service]] and others, and in 1983 he was commissioned to provide specialist microscopic biomedical photography for a [[Channel 4 (UK)|Channel 4]] series, ''The Living Body''.<ref name="soton"/>

Barlow subsequently provided similar photographic work for shows including ''[[Horizon (BBC TV series)|Horizon]]'' and ''[[Equinox (TV programme)|Equinox]]'', as well as working on the BBC's 1998 series ''[[The Human Body (TV series)|The Human Body]]'', for which Barlow received a [[BAFTA]] nomination for Best Photography (Factual).<ref name="soton"/> Barlow later helped convert this show to [[IMAX]] for the [[Discovery Channel]].<ref name="soton"/> Other TV work included the BBC's ''[[Fight for Life (TV series)|Fight for Life]]'' (2007), and Channel 4's ''Extraordinary Animals in the Womb'', about animals with unusual birth procedures, which Barlow recreated using silicon models and computer-aided graphics, and edited together with images captured on 35mm film via a microscope.<ref name="soton"/>

In September 2008 Barlow was awarded an [[Emmy Award]] for Outstanding Individual Achievement in a Craft by the [[National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences]] for his photographic sequences featured in [[National Geographic (U.S. TV channel)|National Geographic]]'s ''Inside the Living Body''.<ref name="soton"/> Due to other work commitments, Barlow was unable to collect the award in person, so his co-nominee Steve Gomez, responsible for computer animation on the project, collected the award on his behalf.<ref name="soton"/> Barlow has also received the [[Lennart Nilsson Award]] for outstanding scientific photography.<ref name="soton"/>
